ma-public-benefit-fraud-auditor-report-2.excerpt: A new state report says investigators identified fraudulent overpayments in 402 cases from January through June, while agencies had finalized $285,339 in civil recoveries and restitution settlements.
ma-public-benefit-fraud-auditor-report-2.text: massachusetts auditor identifies $10.6m in public-benefit fraud, reports limited recoveries a new state report says investigators identified fraudulent overpayments in 402 cases from january through june, while agencies had finalized $285,339 in civil recoveries and restitution settlements. massachusetts state auditor diana dizoglio's office said wednesday that its bureau of special investigations identified $10.6 million in public-benefit fraud during the first six months of 2026, a finding that puts new numbers around losses in programs used for health care, food assistance and family support. the report covers january 1 through june 30 and is based on investigations completed by the bureau, not on criminal convictions in every case. (https://www.mass.gov/news/auditor-dizoglios-bureau-of-special-investigations-identifies-over-106-million-in-public-benefit-fraud) the bureau investigated 2,223 cases during the period and calculated overpayments in 402 cases where it identified fraud, according to the state auditor's report. masshealth and medicaid accounted for the largest share: $6,051,185, or 57% of the total. the supplemental nutrition assistance program accounted for another $3,854,119, or 36.3%. personal care attendant services represented $538,332, followed by $130,483 in transitional aid to families with dependent children and $38,463 in emergency aid to the elderly, disabled, and children. the categories add up to $10,612,582. the distribution matters because the reported losses touch programs with different administrators and different kinds of eligibility records. masshealth helps pay for medical care, snap helps eligible households buy food, and cash-assistance programs support families or people facing emergencies. a finding of an improper payment does not by itself establish who caused it or whether a criminal case will follow; the report describes the bureau's investigative findings and overpayment calculations, while other agencies handle enforcement and collection. the pace of identified fraud was higher than in the preceding six-month reporting period. boston 25 news, reviewing the new report, said the auditor's office had identified about $4.4 million in the prior period. the station also reported that the latest total included two dental providers accused of billing masshealth for “impossible days,” including days when their offices were closed. the report does not name suspected fraudsters, and the figures should be read as a snapshot of cases completed during the reporting period rather than a complete measure of all improper payments in massachusetts. (https://cmg-cmg-tv-10020-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/news/local/25-investigates-106m-benefits-fraud-little-clawed-back/tdd6wuwflre3xau536qiw6ac5a/) the state's recovery figures are much smaller than the amount identified. the report lists $285,339 in restitution settlements and civil recoveries for the two quarters combined, roughly 2.7% of the $10.6 million identified. that comparison does not mean the remaining amount is permanently unrecoverable: the auditor says restitution settlements continue beyond the report, and the programs that administer the benefits are responsible for collection activity. the lag does show why an investigation announcement and a completed recovery are different stages of public accountability. the quarterly split also shows where the total accumulated. in the third quarter of the state's fiscal year, the bureau investigated 994 cases and identified fraud in 168 cases, with overpayments totaling $2,981,696. in the fourth quarter, it investigated 1,229 cases and identified fraud in 234 cases, with overpayments totaling $7,630,886. the report says the fourth-quarter figures include the resumption of referrals through the document benefit fraud task force and two dental-provider cases involving alleged billing for impossible days. the bureau of special investigations operates within the office of the state auditor and can investigate allegations involving programs administered by the department of transitional assistance, the department of children and families and the division of medical assistance, which runs masshealth. its authority does not include collecting settlements or prosecuting cases. those decisions move to the relevant benefit programs and, when appropriate, state or federal prosecutors. boston 25 reported that the executive office of health and human services defended its program-integrity processes while saying agencies had referred most of the cases to the auditor's office. for residents, the report's immediate significance is less about a single statewide bill than about how quickly suspected overpayments are detected, referred and recovered. the auditor's office is asking people with information about possible public-assistance fraud to use its anonymous reporting channels, including the bureau of special investigations hotline at (617) 727-6771. the next measurable steps will be agency decisions on disqualification, civil recoupment or prosecution, along with any future reports showing how much of the identified money is ultimately recovered. massachusetts nyc-trick-or-streets-160-car-free-2026-0.excerpt: The citywide Halloween program will bring free activities, school events and neighborhood walking tours to Open Streets and plazas across all five boroughs.
nyc-trick-or-streets-160-car-free-2026-0.text: nyc plans record 160 car-free trick-or-streets locations for october the citywide halloween program will bring free activities, school events and neighborhood walking tours to open streets and plazas across all five boroughs. new york city is expanding its trick-or-streets program to a record 160 car-free open streets and plazas this october, giving families in all five boroughs a month of halloween and fall events instead of a single-night celebration. the city says the locations will host trick-or-treating, face painting, live entertainment and games. the new york city department of transportation also plans to distribute about 75,000 pieces of candy. abc7 new york reported the same announcement wednesday, sept. 30, and described the program as the city's largest trick-or-streets event to date: https://abc7ny.com/post/mayor-mamdani-announces-nycs-largest-trick-streets-new-york/19892758/ the effort is designed around temporary changes to public space. community organizations, schools and cultural groups will turn selected streets and plazas into pedestrian-oriented gathering places, while the municipal art society of new york will offer free guided walking tours focused on neighborhood history, architecture and public spaces. street lab is also partnering with nyc dot and city schools on halloween-themed play and creative activities at selected school sites. five signature events anchor the schedule. brooklyn's hillel plaza celebration is set for oct. 22 from 2 to 6 p.m.; staten island's water street open street follows oct. 24 from noon to 5 p.m.; and queens' austin street open street is scheduled for oct. 25 from 2 to 7 p.m. manhattan's canal street open street and division plaza event is planned for oct. 28 from 3 to 7 p.m., while the bronx's james baldwin plaza event is scheduled for halloween, oct. 31, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. the department of transportation's event page lists additional neighborhood programs beginning oct. 3, including activities on vanderbilt avenue in brooklyn and castleton avenue on staten island. the calendar includes block parties, parades, dog events and school-linked programming throughout the month. nyc dot says individual events can be delayed or canceled because of weather, so families should check the official calendar before traveling: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/pedestrians/trickorstreets.shtml the month-long format matters because the program is also a test of how new york uses streets beyond their usual transportation role. the city's announcement says the participating groups will use the spaces for community celebrations and, in some cases, to support local foot traffic and neighborhood businesses. the setup gives organizers control over their own programming while the city coordinates the street closures and works with partner agencies. mayor zohran kwame mamdani and nyc dot commissioner mike flynn announced the expansion on sept. 30. this is the fifth year of trick-or-streets, according to nyc dot, which says the initiative is meant to add pedestrian space during one of the busiest periods for new york streets. the full map and schedule remain the best guide to what is happening on a particular block, because the 160 locations will not all be active at the same time. the primary announcement is available from the nyc mayor's office: https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2026/09/mayor-mamdani-announces-largest-ever-trick-or-streets-with-160-c new-york new-york new york ny new york new york
